record.paper_title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
record.original_question: In open polygonal billiards, is the asymptotic survival probability P(t) as t tends to infinity entirely determined by neighborhoods of non-escaping periodic orbits?

evidence.quote: In [30] it was found numerically that P(t) decayed as C/t in an irrational polygonal billiard where at least one periodic orbit was present, and vanished at finite time in a directional flow for a rational polygonal billiard containing no periodic orbits.
Open problem 7. Is the asymptotic survival probability P(t) as t → ∞ in polygonal billiards entirely determined by the neighbourhoods of non-escaping periodic orbits?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a polygon in $\mathbb{R}^2$, possibly with one or several edges (or open subsets of edges) designated as "holes." A billiard trajectory in $P$ is the path of a point particle moving with unit speed in straight lines inside $P$ and reflecting elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) on the non-hole portion of $\partial P$. A trajectory escapes if it meets a hole; otherwise it survives forever. Equip the phase space (unit tangent bundle over $P$) with the standard Liouville measure $\mu$, normalized to be a probability measure on the set of initial conditions. Define the survival probability
$$P(t) = \mu\big(\{(x,v) : \text{the trajectory starting at }(x,v)\text{ has not escaped by time }t\}\big).$$
A periodic orbit of the closed billiard in $P$ is called non-escaping if it (and a neighborhood of it in phase space) avoids the holes for all times.

Question: Is the asymptotic behavior of $P(t)$ as $t \to \infty$ entirely determined by the dynamics in arbitrarily small phase-space neighborhoods of the set of non-escaping periodic orbits? Equivalently, do the neighborhoods of non-escaping periodic orbits give the leading-order contribution to $P(t)$ as $t \to \infty$ for every open polygonal billiard?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is stated as an explicit open problem in surveys on open billiards. Numerical evidence in irrational polygons indicates a $C/t$ decay attributable to periodic orbits, and in rational polygons without periodic orbits the survival ends in finite time, but no proof in general is known. No recent literature appears to establish or refute the conjecture.
